source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without error.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL preserves raw 0x06/0x22 but uses unsafe sshpass/host-key bypass and supplies only generic high-level output for user confirmation.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly gates on existing watchdog action and recovery, but calls the standard parameterless command/vendor semantics unresolved.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending for watchdog semantics, exact request/response, armed state and recovery. IPMI section 27.5 fully defines raw 0x06/0x22 as a parameterless start/restart from the configured initial countdown, including the pre-timeout restriction and uninitialized 80h completion. The risky existing timer policy and observation bounds are finite run inputs, not missing command semantics.
disposition_reason: Read and approve the complete existing watchdog configuration before action, because 0x22 starts an initialized stopped timer as well as refreshing a running one and can thereby activate its configured pre-timeout/timeout action. After immediate confirmation, issue the standard parameterless request once, use Get Watchdog Timer 0x25 to prove the countdown reloaded near the initial value and then decreases, and prove configuration/host state did not otherwise change. Never initialize, stop, reconfigure or retry as fallback.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1000, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1001 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1001 / variant e8dadb024eea3985.

IPMI v2.0 section 27.5 defines Reset Watchdog Timer as starting or restarting from the initial countdown previously set by Set Watchdog Timer; it has no request data and only completion response, with 80h recommended for uninitialized timer.

If the pre-timeout interrupt interval has already been reached, Reset does not restart the timer and only Set can stop it. Therefore the pre-read countdown, pre-timeout interval and independently observed timing are safety gates, not an invitation to use Set as recovery.

Section 27.7 defines Get Watchdog Timer fields and states initial and present countdown should match immediately after Reset, subject to up to 100 ms internal reflection delay. This supplies an objective postcondition beyond source command success.

ED-06, ED-15 through ED-19, ED-26 through ED-28 and ED-30 require one approved state-changing action, host evidence and recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 allow Project-bound existing policy/timing without retaining Pending and prohibit fallback Set or retry.

test_case.test_name: Start or restart the existing in-band IPMI watchdog once and verify countdown reload
test_case.purpose: Verify one standard Reset Watchdog Timer request reloads the exact target's already initialized watchdog from its configured initial countdown, leaves all configuration fields unchanged and causes no unexpected host action during the bounded observation window.
required_package: Immutable DUT/BMC/local-IPMI mapping, pinned firmware/ipmitool/parser/Script and approved support for raw App command 0x22
Strict Get Watchdog 0x06/0x25 parser capturing running bit, timer use/logging, timeout action, pre-timeout interrupt/interval, expiration flags, initial and present countdown in 100 ms units
Approved existing timer policy, including whether starting a stopped initialized timer is intended, safe remaining-time margin before pre-timeout/expiry and expected completion map including 80h
Host workload/power/boot and BMC management observer, maintenance window, independent OOB/console recovery and point-of-action approval
Bounded immediate readback allowing up to the normative 100 ms reflection delay plus a second observation proving decrement, preserved logs and no-retry audit
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind the exact target and preserve logs. Read raw 0x06/0x25 and strictly decode the complete watchdog baseline. Reject uninitialized/reserved/ambiguous fields, a near/pre-timeout condition, unsafe initial value including zero, unapproved pre-timeout/timeout action, unknown stopped-versus-running intent, protected workload or missing recovery. After immediate approval send exactly one protected local `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x22`; capture completion and require no response payload. If completion is 80h or nonzero, stop without Set/retry. Within the approved sampling window, read 0x25, allow up to 100 ms for reflection, prove present countdown reloaded near initial and then decrements, prove the running state matches the approved intent, and compare every configuration/expiration field plus host power/boot/workload and management health to baseline. Do not clear logs, Set/stop/reconfigure the timer, reset/power the host or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The one 0x22 request completes successfully; the initialized watchdog starts/restarts at its unchanged initial countdown, a timely 0x25 readback shows present count equal or within the justified sampling decrement and a later sample decreases monotonically. Timer use/action/pre-timeout/initial value and expiration flags remain unchanged, and host/BMC/workload state has no unexpected transition.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target and immediate approval, a fully decoded safe baseline, exactly one 0x06/0x22 request, completion 00 with no unexpected payload, objective countdown reload/decrement and unchanged policy/flags/host state. Command success alone, uninitialized 80h, Set fallback, a stopped timer started without explicit intent, pre-timeout already reached, zero/unsafe timeout, configuration drift, unexpected interrupt/reset or missing recovery cannot pass. Missing Project policy is NOT READY rather than Pending.
safety_gate: Require point-of-action confirmation after showing exact timer use, running state, initial/present countdown, pre-timeout and timeout actions plus host/workload/recovery state.
Do not act if the timer is uninitialized, at/inside the pre-timeout boundary, uses reserved/unknown fields, has zero/unsafe initial count or an unapproved disruptive action.
Use only parameterless raw 0x06/0x22 on the bound local device; deny Set 0x24, chassis reset/power, BMC reset and arbitrary raw commands.
Preserve watchdog/event/host logs and expiration flags. Do not clear evidence or use Set to clear flags/stop the timer as part of this case.
Use independent OOB/console and host observers; stop on unexpected interrupt, reboot/reset, power/boot change, management loss or configuration drift.
No automatic retry. Any stop/reconfiguration or host recovery requires a separately approved incident action and cannot count as this result.
expected_evidence: Approval, exact DUT/BMC/local-IPMI identity and pinned firmware/tool/parser/Script versions
Complete pre-command raw 0x25 decode, timer-policy approval, safe timing margin, host/workload baseline and recovery readiness
Raw 0x22 request, IPMI completion/response framing and timestamp
Immediate and subsequent raw 0x25 values proving reload then decrement with all configuration/flag comparisons
Host power/boot/workload and BMC-health continuity, preserved logs, no-Set/no-clear/no-retry audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On nonzero completion, failed reload, unexpected action or host impact, stop without 0x22 retry, Set, reset or power fallback and retain all watchdog/host evidence. Use the independent OOB/console incident process; only the owner may separately authorize a standards-compliant Set Watchdog action to stop/restore the timer after evaluating the remaining countdown and host safety.

source_conflict.reason: The Master name and raw 0x06/0x22 align with the standard start/restart command. Missing current policy and postcondition are safely supplied by parameterized baseline/readback, not an authoritative conflict.

blocked.reason: IPMI defines the parameterless operation, errors and verifiable countdown effect. Existing timer policy, safe timing margin, approval and recovery are finite Project prerequisites.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Sections 27.5 and 27.7 define start/restart semantics, pre-timeout restriction, uninitialized 80h completion, complete readback and the countdown reload plus up-to-100-ms reflection rule.

project_authority: The Project owner approves the pre-existing watchdog policy, whether a stopped initialized timer may be started, safe timing margin, host workload and observation/recovery window. It cannot redefine 0x22, use it before initialization or authorize automatic Set/retry fallback inside this case.
